thread:
Sara (CS): FYI customer reported a fairly clear quality regression after yesterday's model rollout. They say hallucinations increased for slot-filling prompts. Customer provided 'before' vs 'after' examples.

Oliver (SRE): Which rollout specifically? dedicated or hosted? model / profile ids?

Sara (CS): Hosted, model id `rw-1b-v2`. Quant profile was changed from `fp16-default` -> `int8-aggressive-2026-03` during the rollout. Customer says their prompt that used to output a short factual list now spits unrelated items.

Tina (ML): :eyes: can you paste the exact customer prompt + both outputs? and any request metadata (max_tokens, temperature, stop)?

Sara (CS): Sure, pasted below. They set temp=0.2, max_tokens=120.
```
Customer prompt: "List the top 3 compliance checks required for onboarding a new EU merchant. Provide short bullets and cite sources where applicable."
Before (fp16-default): "- KYC verification: collect government ID and proof of address (GDPR note: store minimal PII) [gov.uk guidance]\n- AML screening: run sanctions & PEP checks using provider X\n- Data processing agreement: ensure DPA signed with third-party processors\nSources: https://gov.uk/..., https://ec.europa.eu/..."
After (int8-aggressive-2026-03): "- Pancake recipe: mix eggs and flour\n- Contact support for database migration\n- Use vendor Z for shipping"
```

Tina (ML): Oof that's a big semantic break. Sounds like quantization introduced catastrophic degeneration for this pattern. Do we have eval-set diffs across rollout?

Josh (Runtime): I can pull token-level probs and KV-cache diff traces if we repro. Need a request id or customer example request timestamp.

Sara (CS): Customer supplied request id `req_44fb9a`. Time 2026-03-01T18:12:03Z (their timezone). They allowed redaction.

Oliver (SRE): I'll check infra first: any OOMs or failure fallback to smaller model? deploy-bot: what changed in the deploy pipeline around that time?

deploy-bot: Deployment event: rollout `rw-1b-v2` quant profile `int8-aggressive-2026-03` promoted to hosted pool `eu-west-2` at 2026-03-01T17:55:00Z by pipeline#382. No fallback triggers detected.

Josh (Runtime): Ok I'm spinning a repro job now against prod config using the customer's prompt and temp=0.2. Will capture logits and top-k tokens per step.

Tina (ML): Also try with `fp16-default` and `int8-safe-2026-02` for comparison. If int8-safe matches fp16 and aggressive diverges, we can blame the aggressive profile.

Anna (Product): Heads-up: CS escalated to a named account manager; customer is considering pausing calls. We should be fast here.

Sara (CS): +1. Customer is shipping a critical onboarding flow next week.

Josh (Runtime): Repro done. Quick findings: `int8-aggressive-2026-03` outputs the pancake-like tokens after step 12. Token probs show sudden spike to high-prob tokens that are contextually unrelated. I attached a short diff snippet:
```
Step 11 top tokens (fp16-default): ["KYC", "AML", "Data", "-", "Ensure"] (probs 0.18,0.14,0.10,...)
Step 11 top tokens (int8-aggressive): ["pancake", "mix", "ingredients", "-", "Use"] (probs 0.40,0.08,0.05,...)
```

Tina (ML): That smell looks like quantization saturation or per-channel scale mismatch for the attention output kernels. Aggressive profile probably lowered clipping thresholds or merged blocks leading to biased logits. Did the compile change kernel selection?

Josh (Runtime): Yes compile selected an alternative GEMM kernel optimized for int8 per `int8-aggressive` profile. Kernel name: `gemm_int8_vc2_fused`. I have the compiler flags from the job.

Oliver (SRE): Any latency regressions? customer didn't report latency issues; only quality. But check request traces if any retries happened.

Josh (Runtime): No retries. P95 latency stable. Only difference is output distribution.

Tina (ML): Quick mitigation: roll the quant profile back for the hosted pool serving that customer to `int8-safe-2026-02` or `fp16-default` depending on capacity. Can we canary rollback just for that customer or account?

Oliver (SRE): We support routing by account -> can route that account to a `fp16-pool` override in the routing service. Ops can flip a routing rule. Will need 15 min window.

Anna (Product): Do it. Also we should prepare a customer-facing explanation and a postmortem. Keep it succinct: "we rolled an optimization that regressed outputs; we've rolled this account back and are investigating."

Sara (CS): I'll notify the customer that we have a mitigative step pending and ask for permission to route them to fp16 while we investigate.

Josh (Runtime): Action log so far: captured logits + token diffs, noted compiler kernel `gemm_int8_vc2_fused`, confirmed no infra fallback. Next: reproduce locally with unit tests to isolate which op causes bias. Tina to run quant-sensitivity sweep on affected layers.

Tina (ML): Plan: (1) run layerwise dynamic range analysis on `rw-1b-v2` with representative prompts; (2) try per-channel calibration with more calibration samples; (3) run synthetic fusion-disable builds to see if fused kernel is the culprit. ETA 24h for initial results.

Oliver (SRE): I've initiated the routing override for account `acct_8291` -> `fp16-pool-eu`. Change should take effect in ~10m. Noting rollback window and audit id `audit_5402`.

deploy-bot: Routing change applied by Oliver at 2026-03-01T18:22:10Z.

Sara (CS): Customer confirmed they see improved outputs after 8 minutes. They are satisfied for now but want a full explanation.

Anna (Product): Great, let's keep them updated. Tina/Josh—when you have root cause, propose a release schedule for either a safer int8 profile or a guardrail in the compiler to avoid that fused kernel for sensitive layers.

Josh (Runtime): Agreed. Preliminary mitigation we can push: add a config to compiler to blacklist `gemm_int8_vc2_fused` for `rw-*` family until quant-sensitivity tests pass. That can be hot-fixed in the compile controls and pushed to the pool.

Tina (ML): Also propose adding a small online quality check during canary promotion: run a tiny eval set (10 prompts) that checks KL divergence + top-token overlap vs fp16. If divergence > threshold, abort promotion.

Sara (CS): I'll draft the customer note once we have RCA. For now: rollback done, customer happy, action items assigned.

Anna (Product): Putting this on next sprint planning as a must-fix for Dedicated & Hosted parity. Thanks team. :raised_hands:

Oliver (SRE): Filing incident ticket in our tracker for the regression and mitigation steps (INC-2026-089).

Sara (CS): Closing loop with customer and will attach incident id.

Josh (Runtime): Logging attachments: token diffs, compile flags, kernel binary sha. I'll upload to the incident.

Tina (ML): Will share initial quant-sweep results in the incident within 24h.

Sara (CS): Thanks all. We'll reconvene if new customer reports come in.
